title: Form, Structure, and Sense, Part 2: A Hard Question, Traps

beats.say: In part one, we looked at the choices first, to see which rule was being tested.
We crossed out prepositional phrases to find the true subject, and put the doer right after an opening phrase.
beats.item: Find the subject; place the doer

beats.say: In this video, we work through a hard question about tense and pronouns, and then the common traps.
beats.item: Today: a hard question and traps

beats.say: Hard question. Tense follows time clues. If a sentence gives a past date, the verb must be in the past. If one past action happened before another, use the past perfect.

card.sub: Earlier past action: had plus participle

beats.say: Also check each pronoun. A company, a team, or a museum is one thing, so it takes it and its, not they and their.

scenes.title: Read the sentence
scenes.text: By the time the museum reopened in 2019, its curators ______ every painting in the east wing and had moved the collection to a new climate-controlled room.

beats.say: The time clue is, by the time the museum reopened in twenty nineteen. The curators finished their work before that date.
beats.underline: By the time the museum reopened

beats.say: The second verb, had moved, is in the past perfect. The first verb is joined by and, so it must match it, and it needs a past participle.

scenes.title: Which verb fits?
scenes.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

beats.say: Choice A, cleaned, is the simple past. It does not show that the cleaning happened before the reopening, and it does not match had moved.
Choice C, were cleaning, shows an action in progress. The sentence needs a finished action before the reopening.
Choice D, will clean, is the future. The sentence gives a past date, so a future verb is wrong.
Choice B, had cleaned, is the past perfect. It matches had moved, and the earlier action. The answer is B.
Now the traps. Each one is a way that a careful reader can still pick a wrong answer. We will see the trap, and then the habit that avoids it.
Trap one. Students make the verb agree with the noun closest to it. But that noun is often inside a phrase.
beats.wrong: The collection of maps are old

beats.say: Cross out the phrase, and agree with the true subject. The collection is singular.
beats.right: The collection of maps is old

beats.say: Trap two. Some subjects sound plural but are singular. Each of the students, the number of cases, and the team are all singular.
beats.wrong: Each of the students are ready

beats.say: Find the head word of the subject. Each is singular, so the verb is singular.
beats.right: Each of the students is ready

beats.say: Trap three. A company, a school, or a city is a single thing. Students often write they or their for it.
beats.wrong: The company said they would hire

beats.say: Use it and its for a single organization, and match the pronoun to the noun.
beats.right: The company said it would hire

beats.say: Trap four. An apostrophe does not make a plural. Sale apostrophe s is wrong when you only mean more than one sale.
Use a plain s for a plural, and use an apostrophe only to show that something belongs to someone.
Trap five. After had or was, use the past participle. Had wrote and was wrote are wrong.
Use had written. The simple past, wrote, stands alone, but had needs the participle.
To recap. Cross out phrases, find the true subject, and watch for singular words that sound plural.
Use the time clue for tense, it for one organization, and the past participle after had. That completes all the topics, so now practice them.
